sources.title: Luís Fróis, Jesuit missionary letters and Historia de Japam — independent European firsthand observation of Hideyoshi's court
Hideyoshi's own surviving letters to his wife, One (Nene)
Japanese chronicles and administrative records of the Sword Hunt edict (1588) and land survey program

proactive_agency.rationale: Rose from peasant origins to become the most powerful man in Japan through self-directed military and political achievement in a rigid class society — an extraordinary, well-documented ascent unprecedented for the era.

achievement_drive.rationale: Sustained pursuit of ever-greater power from peasant birth to supreme ruler of a unified Japan, documented across the full, unbroken arc of his career.

decisiveness.rationale: Defeated Oda Nobunaga's assassin, Akechi Mitsuhide, within weeks of the 1582 assassination, seizing the succession opportunity swiftly — a specific, extremely well-documented decisive act at a critical moment.

persuasiveness.rationale: Unified much of Japan substantially through diplomacy and alliance-building with former rivals rather than pure military conquest — a documented strategic approach distinct from his predecessor Nobunaga's.

planning_orientation.rationale: Implemented the 1588 Sword Hunt edict disarming the peasant class and a systematic nationwide land survey — documented, sophisticated administrative planning, not improvised policy.

adaptability.rationale: Adapted successfully from serving under Nobunaga to independently ruling, and adapted his own strategic approach toward diplomacy rather than continuing Nobunaga's purely military conquest style.

risk_tolerance.rationale: Launched two large-scale invasions of Korea (1592, 1597), extraordinarily ambitious campaigns that ultimately failed and caused immense documented suffering — a real risk that did not pay off.

mastery_orientation.rationale: Demonstrated sustained military and administrative skill development from a very low social starting position, documented by his steady rise through progressively greater responsibility under Nobunaga before independent rule.

leadership_drive.rationale: Sustained pursuit and consolidation of supreme power over a unified Japan, documented by the completeness of that unification under his rule.

social_assertiveness.rationale: Sustained direct assertion of authority and status across a career that began from the lowest social rank, evidenced by his documented progressive rise within Nobunaga's own hierarchy.

collaboration.rationale: His surviving personal letters to his wife One document a genuine, sustained relationship, and his unification strategy relied heavily on documented alliance-building with former rivals rather than their elimination alone.

impact_motivation.rationale: Sustained, documented commitment to unifying Japan and establishing lasting social and administrative order (the Sword Hunt and land surveys), extending beyond his own personal rule.

conflict_tolerance.rationale: Sustained decades of military campaigning, culminating in the costly and ultimately unsuccessful Korean invasions — a documented, sustained pattern of accepting large-scale conflict.

independent_thinking.rationale: Developed a distinctly diplomatic and administrative approach to unification, documented as different from Nobunaga's more purely military style — a specific strategic departure, not an inherited template.

ambiguity_tolerance.rationale: Navigated the extraordinarily unstable Sengoku ("Warring States") period for decades to eventual unification, evidenced by the sustained continuity of his rise through that instability.

discipline.rationale: Sustaining a decades-long, incremental rise from peasant origins to supreme power implies real personal discipline, inferred from that overall trajectory rather than a single cited episode.

cross_domain_range.rationale: Functioned with real, documented substantive output as military commander, diplomat, and administrator (including the land survey program and the construction of Osaka Castle) — three genuinely distinct domains.

autonomy_need.rationale: Rose to supreme power despite starting with no inherited status or hereditary claim, building entirely independent authority, inferred from that documented absence of inherited position.

provenance.notes: Roster-13 new-intake batch (2026-09): East Asia pick. Evidence draws on an independent European source (Jesuit missionary Luís Fróis, who observed his court directly) alongside Japanese chronicles and his own surviving personal letters, rather than a single tradition. The failed Korean invasions are scored honestly as a real, documented risk that did not pay off (risk_tolerance), not omitted to protect the profile. Scored to completion before any eligibility check was run.
